title: Per-system credentials manifest
description: ADR-0061 D3, sibling of state-manifest.<system>.json. Declares each secret a restored system needs — its TRANSPORT, not just its inventory (finding 8) — and NEVER its value (P14 / reference-secrets-dont-transmit): only names, pointers, and procedures. Secrets travel through neither git nor backup media by design (D2 leg 3), so this manifest is the answer key `poga restore` prints as the 'incomplete — N credentials to re-provision' checklist. It never carries a value; the schema forbids one structurally (additionalProperties:false with no `value` property). One file per system: `credentials-manifest.<system>.json`.

//.description: Free-text documentation comment. Repo convention. String or list of strings. Never a secret.

system.description: The system-id this manifest belongs to. Must match the `<system>` in this file's name and the state manifest's `system`.

version.description: The manifest-schema version this instance targets (semver).

credentials.description: The secrets a restored system must re-provision. ORDER IS SIGNIFICANT and load-bearing (finding 1): item zero is the root identity (nothing else can be provisioned without it); the next entries are secrets that gate reading the backups themselves (e.g. the offsite encryption key), before any application secret. `restore --plan` renders this list in order as the re-provision checklist. An empty array asserts the system needs NO secrets to authenticate — a positive claim to be verified, not an omission.

name.description: Stable identifier for the secret, e.g. 'root-identity', 'offsite-encryption-key', 'github-access'. Not the value — the name.

transport.description: How the secret gets re-established (finding 8). 'human-only' = no machine injection possible; `restore` prints a guided checklist and a human performs it (interactive device flows, web logins, the root identity, the offsite encryption key). 'machine-injectable' = a fetch-at-use helper can supply it (a controller-served endpoint) so the value never lands in a transcript. A 'human-only' entry is a term in the 'incomplete — N to re-provision' count; it is why restore never reports plain success (D2).

required_for.description: Optional. What this credential unblocks — data_source names from the state manifest, or a short phrase (e.g. 'reading the offsite backup'). Lets `restore --plan` show why a missing credential blocks a given leg.

provision.description: Ordered steps to RE-ESTABLISH the secret — a procedure, never the secret itself. For 'human-only': the guided checklist (where to go, which identity, what to do). For 'machine-injectable': the controller-served endpoint pattern to fetch it at use. Where a step would name a value, it names a POINTER instead (reference-secrets-dont-transmit). Order is significant.
